readMe: The numbers that change a decision without belonging to any rule.
`session-rules.json` holds every threshold the session decision engine
applies, and each one is owned by a rule that declares what it cuts and
what it rests on. These are the other kind: constants inside the state
computation that no rule owns, that appear in no `decisionBasis`, and that
the caller therefore never sees — and that change what the engine decides
all the same. A detraining flag, a divisor under an HRV reading, and the
age at which a reading stops describing today are all of that kind.
They lived as bare literals in three source files until 2026-08-08. Moving
them here does not make them better evidenced; it makes the absence of
evidence visible in the same shape as everywhere else. Every one of them
is `internal_composite` with no sources, and that is the honest reading,
not an oversight to be filled in later with something plausible.
The engines read their values from this file, the same arrangement as the
rule library: editing a `value` here changes what Evidra computes. The
join is guarded in both directions by `assertParametersMatch` — a key the
engine reads that nothing here declares fails at load, and so does a
parameter nobody applies.
Not covered here yet, and named so the gap is not mistaken for a claim of
completeness: the CTL/ATL time constants (42 and 7), the TSB bands, the
recovery-score weights, the readiness penalty coefficients, the plan phase
multipliers and the plan return ramp are all still bare literals in their
own files.
1.1.0, on 2026-08-09: EVD-P-001 and EVD-P-002 left. The detraining pair
gated EVD-R-007 — they decided whether that rule fired at all — so holding
them here put the trigger a tier below the rule and kept it out of the
decisionBasis the rule does reach. They are now that rule's own thresholds
in session-rules.json, at the same values. Nothing here is retired for being
wrong; this one moved because it turned out to belong to a rule.

groups.label: When a break counts as detraining
The reference values raw recovery readings are scored against
How old a reading may be and still describe today

parameters.title: HRV reference used when the athlete has no baseline of their own
parameters.definition: The divisor in the HRV recovery signal: signal = clamp(hrv / baseline x 100). A reading equal to the baseline scores 100.
parameters.appliedIn: calculateRecoveryScore, and so in recovery, readiness, and every readiness threshold the rule library cuts.
limitations: 52 has no stated origin in this repo and no citation behind it.

HRV varies by measurement method, time of day and individual by more than the differences this number is being used to detect, so a fixed divisor makes one athlete's normal night look like another's bad one. It is a fallback, and a per-athlete baseline supplied by the caller supersedes it.
It sits underneath a readiness score that rules then cut at 40, 60 and 75, so an error here moves those cut points without any of them changing.

parameters.title: Resting heart rate reference used when the athlete has no baseline of their own
parameters.definition: The reference in the resting-heart-rate signal: signal = clamp(100 - max(0, restingHr - baseline) x 5). At or below the baseline the signal is 100; every beat above costs 5 points.
parameters.appliedIn: calculateRecoveryScore, and so in recovery and readiness.
limitations: 57 has no stated origin in this repo and no citation behind it.
The penalty slope of 5 points per beat is a separate ungoverned literal in the same expression, and it decides how much this baseline matters.

parameters.title: Assumed weekly training load when the athlete's history is too short for their own
parameters.definition: Stands in for observed chronic weekly load while the 28-day window is too thin to supply one, and so sits in the denominator of the crude acute:chronic ratio.
parameters.appliedIn: calculateTrainingLoad. The decision chain supersedes the crude ratio with the impulse-response one once history has converged, so this reaches a decision only on short histories — which is exactly when it is least testable.
limitations: 360 has no stated origin in this repo and no citation behind it.
A ratio measured against an assumed target is already reported to the caller as provisional in `limits`; that sentence is the only place this number is visible from outside.

parameters.title: How old a sleep reading may be
parameters.definition: A reading older than this is dropped rather than used, and the signal is reported in signalCoverage.recovery.missing instead.
limitations: 3 is our own choice with no citation behind it.
It decides which side of the missing/usable line a sparse wearer's night falls on, so it moves confidence and — through the recovery weights — readiness.

parameters.title: How old an HRV or stress reading may be
parameters.definition: A reading older than this is dropped rather than used, and the signal is reported in signalCoverage.recovery.missing instead.
limitations: 7 is our own choice with no citation behind it.
A week-old HRV reading is admitted at full weight (0.35) rather than discounted by age, so this is a cliff rather than a decay.

parameters.title: How old a resting heart rate reading may be
parameters.definition: A reading older than this is dropped rather than used, and the signal is reported in signalCoverage.recovery.missing instead.
limitations: 14 is our own choice with no citation behind it. It is the longest window here, on the reasoning that resting heart rate moves more slowly than the other three — reasoning, not measurement.

parameters.title: How old a vendor composite score may be
parameters.definition: A composite older than this is dropped rather than used. Shorter than the raw signals because these scores are the vendor's statement about a particular day rather than a measurement that ages.
limitations: 2 is our own choice with no citation behind it.

These composites carry the heaviest weights in the recovery score (0.4, 0.3 and 0.25), so this window decides whether recovery is scored mostly by the vendor or mostly by us — and, where no raw signal is present at all, whether it is scored at all.
